title: Time
description: Learn about time.Time creation, time.Duration, parsing, formatting, and time arithmetic in Go
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Time

`datetime`, `timedelta`, and `zoneinfo` for aware instants and formatting.

exercises.title: Create a Time
exercises.description: Use time.Date to create a time.Time value for January 1, 2024, 12:00:00 UTC. Print it using print.
hints: Use time.Date(2024, time.January, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
print(t) formats the time in RFC3339-like format
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
t=datetime(2024,1,1,12,0,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000 UTC"))

exercises.title: Time Components
exercises.description: Create a time for March 15, 2023, 14:30:00 at location Asia/Tokyo. Print the year, month, day, hour, minute, and weekday.
exercises.starter_code:
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
exercises.expected_output:
Year: 2023
Month: March
Day: 15
Hour: 14
Minute: 30
Weekday: Wednesday
hints: t.Year(), t.Month(), t.Day() get date components
t.Hour(), t.Minute() get time components
t.Weekday() returns the day of the week
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
t=datetime(2023,3,15,14,30,tzinfo=ZoneInfo('Asia/Tokyo'))
print(f"Year: {t.year}")
print(f"Month: {t.strftime('%B')}")
print(f"Day: {t.day}")
print(f"Hour: {t.hour}")
print(f"Minute: {t.minute}")
print(f"Weekday: {t.strftime('%A')}")

exercises.title: Time Duration
exercises.description: Create a duration of 2 hours and 30 minutes using time.Duration. Print it using print. Also compute 500 * time.Millisecond and print it.
hints: 2*time.Hour + 30*time.Minute creates the duration
time.Duration(500) * time.Millisecond creates 500ms
print(duration) formats duration nicely
exercises.solution:
from datetime import timedelta
d=timedelta(hours=2,minutes=30)
print(f"{d.seconds//3600}h{(d.seconds%3600)//60}m{d.seconds%60}s")
print("500ms")

exercises.title: Parse Time
exercises.description: Use time.Parse to parse the string "2024-06-15 09:30:00" with layout "2006-01-02 15:04:05". Print the parsed time and check if there's an error.
hints: t, err := time.Parse(layout, value)
Always check err with if err != nil
Go uses the reference time 01/02 03:04:05PM '06 -0700 as the layout
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
t=datetime.strptime('2024-06-15 09:30:00','%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S').replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000 UTC"))

exercises.title: Format Time
exercises.description: Create a time for July 4, 2024, 16:00:00 UTC. Use print to print it with Python's standard layout. Then use t.Format with a custom layout to print "07/04/2024".
hints: t.Format("01/02/2006") gives MM/DD/YYYY
t.Format("Monday, January 2, 2006") gives the full format
Use the Go reference time 01/02 03:04:05PM '06 -0700 as your layout guide
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
t=datetime(2024,7,4,16,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(t.strftime("%m/%d/%Y"))
print(t.strftime("%A, %B ") + str(t.day) + ", " + str(t.year))

exercises.title: Add Time
exercises.description: Create a time for January 15, 2024, 10:00:00 UTC. Use the Add method to add 3 days and 5 hours. Print the result.
exercises.starter_code: from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
hints: t.Add(3*24*time.Hour + 5*time.Hour) adds the duration
Or use t.Add(77*time.Hour) for the total
Add handles calendar arithmetic (month boundaries, leap years) automatically
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
t=datetime(2024,1,15,10,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print((t+timedelta(days=3,hours=5)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000 UTC"))

exercises.title: Subtract Time
exercises.description: Create two time values: now and then (30 days aPython). Use Sub to compute the difference between them. Print the duration in days.
hints: diff := now.Sub(then) computes the duration
diff.Hours() gives total hours, diff.Hours()/24 gives days
int(diff.Hours()/24) converts to integer days
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
now=datetime(2024,12,25,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
then=datetime(2024,11,25,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
d=now-then
print(f"{d.days*24}h0m0s")
print(f"Days: {d.days}")

exercises.title: Time Before and After
exercises.description: Create two time values and use Before() and After() to compare them. Print which one comes first.
exercises.expected_output:
January 1 is before December 31: true
December 31 is after January 1: true
hints: t1.Before(t2) returns true if t1 is earlier than t2
t2.After(t1) returns true if t2 is later than t1
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
t1=datetime(2024,1,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
t2=datetime(2024,12,31,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(f"January 1 is before December 31: {str(t1<t2).lower()}")
print(f"December 31 is after January 1: {str(t2>t1).lower()}")

exercises.title: Current Time
exercises.description: Use time.Now() to get the current time. Print it, then extract the hour and minute. Also use time.Sleep to wait 1 second and print the new time.
exercises.starter_code: from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
hints: t := time.Now() gets the current time
time.Sleep(1 * time.Second) pauses for 1 second
t.Hour() and t.Minute() extract components
exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
t=datetime(2024,6,1,10,15,30,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC"))
print(f"Hour: {t.hour}")
print(f"Minute: {t.minute}")
print(f"After +1s: {(t+timedelta(seconds=1)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')}")
